transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-31
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mora (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Ben Holt (Redwood Solutions Eng); Jasmine Park (Sierra Logistics), Marcus Lee (Infra), Tanya Rivera (PM)
Links shared: https://redwood.ai/deck/console-walkthrough (deck), https://redwood.ai/security/soc2.pdf (security pack)

Summary: Brief console demo focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown per model/route. Customer interested in using Dedicated capacity for low-latency shipments scoring and wants clarity on token-level cost, KV cache benefits, and VPC/private deployment options. Discussed pilot scope and next steps to run a benchmark.

Topics: usage analytics, per-route cost, routing policies, Dedicated vs Hosted, VPC and SOC2, audit logs, rollout policies, pilot benchmarking

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: okay uh hey everyone thanks for joining uh i'm alex with Redwood Inference, i'll kick off
 um Priya's gonna run the console demo, Ben's on for any infra deep dive later.
[00:12] Jasmine: thanks Alex, excited to see the console, we had a few questions on per-route cost and how we'd measure savings.
[00:20] Priya: great, i'll share my screen — give me one sec, ok can you see the console?
[00:27] Marcus: yep looks good, screen is shared.
[00:30] Priya: perfect. So first slide is the usage analytics home, this is token-level breakdown by model and route, we show p50/p95 latency and cost per 1k tokens, and you can filter by time range, team, and route. you can also pin certain routes to watch.
[00:50] Tanya: when you say route, do you mean api route in our app? like /scoring and /chat?
[00:56] Priya: yes exactly, per-route maps to your API endpoint or use-case. so for example here we have shipments-scoring, chat-support, and summarizer. each route has its own cost curve and model mapping.
[01:10] Priya: (points) here's token-level cost — notice the delta between hosted small model and dedicated quantized model, this is where Redwood Optimize recommendations kick in. sometimes the console suggests a quantization profile and batching rule.
[01:28] Jasmine: slight transcription glitch: you said quantization 'profile' — is that safe for accuracy-sensitive scoring?
[01:34] Priya: good question. the recommendations show expected perf delta and a quality risk flag; for scoring we usually recommend int8 or q4 depending on your tolerance. we can run evals on your test prompts.
[01:45] [01:46] Ben: also the console ties quality regressions to prompt sets so you can see if quantization introduced drift on specific examples.
[01:52] Marcus: what's the unit economics view? how do you get to dollars?
[01:56] Priya: under the cost tab we show per-route spend, cost per 1k tokens, and predicted monthly spend given traffic. you can toggle reserved capacity discounts for Dedicated to see committed vs on-demand.
[02:12] Priya: quick note — KV cache (sometimes in our docs as KV cash) is shown per-route: cache hit rates reduce token counts downstream, so routes with stable prefixes get big wins.
[02:26] Jasmine: ah that was one of our questions — our scoring requests have a lot of repeated context so sounds promising.
[02:31] Priya: yeah, and you can set prefix caching per route and see the estimated token savings.
[02:38] [03:00] Alex: can you show routing policies? e.g., route to cheaper model for non-critical requests and to Dedicated for low-latency critical calls.
[03:08] Priya: sure — routing tab here. policies can be based on latency SLO, cost preference, region, or customer tier. example: shipments-scoring goes to dedicated-lowlat by default, falls back to hosted-cost if dedicated capacity is full.
[03:26] Marcus: does fallback preserve request semantics? like same model version or do we get different tokenization/outputs?
[03:33] Priya: we do version-aware fallbacks: we try to route to compatible model variants; console flags potential semantic diffs in the rollout UI and you can set automatic fallback or require manual approval.
[03:47] Tanya: do you capture audit logs for these reroutes? our security team needs change history.
[03:52] Priya: yes audit logs include routing decisions, model version changes, and user actions. they can be exported or connected to your SIEM.
[04:00] [04:30] Jasmine: what about VPC/private deployment? Marcus' team will need network diagrams and info on key management.
[04:38] Alex: we already uploaded the SOC2 and private deployment docs link in the chat — but Priya, can you highlight the Private option?
[04:45] Priya: absolutely. Private deployment gives a customer-managed control plane; we support VPC peering and on-prem packages for air-gapped. KMS/HSM integration is supported, and audit logs stay on customer side if you choose that mode.
[05:00] Marcus: latency wise, Dedicated in our region— can you share sample p95 numbers?
[05:06] Priya: for 8k context models on a 4xA100 Dedicated pool we see p95 around 120-180ms for generation-only paths; with KV cache warm and batching it's lower. the per-route dashboard shows p50/p95 plotted historically.
[05:25] Jasmine: a lot of numbers, would you send a one-pager with typical p95 by model family?
[05:30] Alex: yes i'll attach a benchmark sheet; Priya will also share the console clip.
[05:36] [06:00] Priya: switching to the per-route dashboard — you can expand shipments-scoring. here's request volume, latency distribution, model mapping, and a cost waterfall that breaks down token cost, infra premium (dedicated overhead), and caching savings.
[06:18] Priya: note the waterfall is approximate but aligns to invoices; you can download a CSV for financial reconciliation.
[06:26] Marcus: great, can we map this to our billing buckets? we need to attribute spend by product team.
[06:33] Priya: yes the console supports tags and you can slice by team, project, or route. we also have an API to pull these metrics into your internal FinOps tooling.
[06:45] Tanya: about pilot scope — we want a 2-week benchmark against our current self-hosted setup and an SLA for critical path. what's typical?
[06:54] Ben: typical pilot is 2-4 weeks, we run a traffic replay with live traffic shadowing, collect p95, cost/1k token, and quality metrics. at the end we present a cost/latency tradeoff and recommended Dedicated commit.
[07:13] Jasmine: what about data retention and logs — retention is a compliance requirement for us.
[07:19] Priya: retention is configurable per account; we also offer an option to forward logs to your storage. for Private deployments you manage retention entirely.
[07:27] [08:00] Marcus: security checklist — SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption in transit and at rest, SOC2. do you support customer-managed keys?
[08:09] Alex: yes customer-managed KMS is supported in Private and on Dedicated for enterprise, and we support HSM integration for higher compliance tiers.
[08:18] Jasmine: can you confirm whether data used for model updates is retained or used by Redwood?
[08:24] Priya: by default hosted API does not use customer data for model training; for Dedicated and Private, data stays in your environment and isn't used for training. we'll confirm contractual language in the security pack.
[08:35] [09:00] Priya: toggling to Optimize suggestions — here we surface batching, cache, and quantization recommendations per route and show estimated monthly savings. you can preview the savings before applying and run an eval on your prompt set.
[09:15] Marcus: do recommendations come with confidence bands? we need to avoid overpromising cost reductions.
[09:20] Priya: yes each recommendation has a confidence score and expected delta; we also show historical cases where a similar workload saw X% savings.
[09:30] Tanya: is there an API to accept recommendations programmatically?
[09:34] Priya: yes we have an admin API that can apply batching policies and quantization flags; changes go through the rollout system.
[09:40] [11:00] Jasmine: small nit — earlier you mentioned permissions, can we restrict who can apply recommendations?
[11:06] Priya: RBAC is granular — you can restrict by role: view-only, ops, security, or admin. application of changes can require 2-person approval if you like.
[11:20] Marcus: for the pilot we'd want a read-only view for analytics and a small ops group to make changes.
[11:25] Alex: noted, we'll template that.
[11:30] [12:00] Priya: show the rollout panel — you can canary a new model for 5% traffic, compare quality and latency against the prod baseline, and either promote or roll back. the console surfaces drift alerts if outputs diverge.
[12:18] Jasmine: how are drift alerts configured?
[12:21] Priya: linked to your eval sets and production prompts; if a threshold of mismatches is crossed the alert fires and can optionally pause rollout.
[12:30] [14:00] Ben: small comment on telemetry — we emit trace ids that you can correlate with your APM; these are included in the audit export.
[14:10] Marcus: good. one more: cost modeling for reserved capacity — give me an example commit size vs discount curve.
[14:18] Priya: in the pricing tab you can input a commit level and we show expected discount and net monthly cost; for example a 3-month commit on dedicated pool reduces per-token infra premium by ~20% in our sample region.
[14:36] Tanya: do you have references in logistics or retail?
[14:40] Alex: yes, we'll share two anonymized case studies— one logistics customer reduced per-call cost by 35% after caching and quantization.
[14:48] [16:00] Jasmine: ok let's talk about the pilot specifics — what data we need to provide.
[16:06] Ben: we need traffic profile (avg qps, peak qps), token distribution sample, and a set of representative prompts and expected outputs. Marcus will handle infra details.
[16:18] Marcus: i'll send the qps and token dist CSV.
[16:22] Jasmine: timeline — if we run a pilot next week, what's the onboarding time?
[16:27] Priya: onboarding is typically 2-5 business days for a dedicated pilot if credentials and network are ready. Private takes longer.
[16:36] [18:00] Alex: i'm going to recap — action items and next steps. Priya will share the console clip and screenshot pack; Alex to send Dedicated pricing and contract template; Marcus to send traffic CSV; we will schedule pilot kickoff and a 30-minute benchmark planning session.
[18:18] Tanya: sounds good, can we get a proposed date for the kickoff?
[18:22] Alex: i'll propose dates in the next 24 hours.
[18:28] [20:00] Priya: one more note: billing attribution — you can map routes to cost centers and export monthly reports for finance.
[20:08] Marcus: perfect.
[20:12] [22:00] Jasmine: any final security concerns? we've seen in other vendors that logs were incomplete.
[22:07] Alex: understood — we'll include log schema and export samples in the security pack.
[22:13] Priya: and i can loop in our security eng to walk through the SOC2 and KMS flow if needed.
[22:20] [24:00] Ben: i'll follow up with a short infra checklist for the Dedicated pilot (ports, peering, KMS endpoints).
[24:08] Marcus: ok thanks Ben.
[24:12] [26:00] Jasmine: thanks everyone, this was super helpful.
[26:05] Alex: thanks all — we'll follow up with materials. bye.

Recap / Next steps (spoken at end):
- Alex to send Dedicated pricing and sample contract (by 2026-04-02)
- Priya to share per-route dashboard screenshots and a short console video (by 2026-04-01)
- Marcus to provide traffic profile and token distribution CSV (by 2026-04-03)
- Schedule pilot kickoff and benchmark planning session (Alex to propose dates)

End of transcript.
